description: issue #681 (slice I2): a read no host can answer. `spec/interaction-events.md:110-111` gives a blocking read exactly two endings — it runs "until the read finishes or the program is cancelled" — so a headless run with no scripted answer (`executeOptions.hostInput.responses` omitted) takes the second. It reaches that ending through the profile`s ordinary cancellation diagnostic, identical in code, params AND message to an externally cancelled run: diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and prose is presentation (`spec/error-model.md:235-238`), so a lookalike diagnostic with its own wording would make the message stop being a function of the identity and be unreachable in a localized build. What localizes it to this instruction is the SPAN, which covers the waiting `input` call rather than the whole statement. `spec/interaction-events.md:352` sanctions `ol-limit` here ("an instruction budget or cancellation limit was reached"). The program stops at the read, so the following `print` never runs and no `primitive` event is emitted — reporting an invented answer (an empty word, say) instead would let the program run on as though the learner had answered, a silent wrong result, which is exactly what a diagnostic exists to prevent.

diagnostics.message: execution was cancelled before the program finished.
